page.layout: One column of running text, with the printed page number and running head at the top. Left and right edges show faint fragments of the neighbouring page and show-through, which are omitted. Two faint marks at the bottom right, beside the last line, are probably show-through from the reverse side and are omitted.

main_text.p: sepolita ad tempus, veste, comitatu, moribus quasi civis Atticus inter cives versabatur, omnibusque familiarem se dabat, reipublicæ quoque munera nonnunquàm gerebat, eoque honore velut gaudere videbatur. Et accidit aliquan-dò, cum esset Antonius Athenis, & secum duceret Cleopatram suam, arma æmulo suo Cæsari Octaviano illaturus, intereaq; dum bello necessaria pararen-tur, more suo ludis & theatris se daret, accidit, inquam, ut Cleopatra cognoscens maximis honoribus Octaviam Antonii conjugem ab Athenien-sibus non multò ante cultam fuisse, ostende-ret, pares honores se quoque ab iis defi-derare.Cumque in gratiam Antonii, cujus mentè bene norat, honores illi eosdem civitas decrevisset, legatosque, qui decretum illi adferrent, domum ejus mitteret, ipse Antonius, ut affirmat Plutarchus, inter eos esse voluit, utpote qui civis Atticus esset, idemque coram regina stans nomine civitatis verba ad eam fecit. δράμα [?] fanè risu dignum.

Verum haud diu post victus ad Actium, fugaque elapsus cum Cleopatrâ, & in Ægyptum reversus, deficientibus amicis de fortuna jam desperans legatos ex voluntate Cleopatræ misit ad Cæsarem victorem, petiitque ut regnum Ægypti

page.notes: The Greek word after "verba ad eam fecit." is printed as a single Greek word, read here as δράμα with [?] because the letters are faint. Printed "derare.Cumque" has no space after the full stop; kept as printed. The word "fanè" carries a grave accent as printed. No catchword is clearly visible at the foot; the page ends mid-sentence at "Ægypti". Faint marks at the lower right ("libc", "mœm") are judged to be show-through and are left out.
